title: An ALMA and MagAO Study of the Substellar Companion GQ Lup B*
question: What are the properties of the dust disks around GQ Lup A and its substellar companion GQ Lup B, and what do they imply for the formation and orbit of GQ Lup B?

what.value: Gas mass of 71.3 +/- 8.3 Earth masses used for total disk mass

evidence.quote: Total mass is calculated by adding our dust mass to the gas mass of 71.3 $\pm$ 8.3 $M_\ensuremath{\oplus}$ measured by (cite: M16).

what.value: Disk radius of 46.5 AU from CO (3-2) used for tidal truncation analysis

evidence.quote: We adopt a disk radius of 46.5 AU determined by (cite: M16) from CO (3–2) emission

what.value: Orbit groups (a, e, i) of GQ Lup B

evidence.quote: showed that the semi-major axis $a$, eccentricity $e$, and inclination $i$ of GQ Lup B’s orbit fall into three groups

recipe.method: CASA calibration, MSMFS CLEAN with natural weighting, four rounds of phase-only self-calibration

recipe.goal: Upper limit on GQ Lup B disk mass
recipe.method: Inject fake sources in 0.1" region, find 99.7% recovery flux per disk size, convert to dust mass with optically thin formula
assumptions: T = 20 K, kappa(1.3 mm) = 2.3 cm2/g, distance 150 pc

recipe.goal: Fit GQ Lup A disk visibilities
recipe.method: RADMC-3D radiative transfer models (power-law Model A and Lynden-Bell & Pringle Model B), Fourier transformed and fit to visibilities
assumptions: 70% silicate/30% graphite, grain size 5 nm to 3 mm, power-law -3.5, giving 2.25 cm2/g at 1.3 mm

recipe.goal: MagAO photometry of GQ Lup B
recipe.method: ADI+KLIP with grid search over parameters using injected fake planets; fake-planet injection for i', z', Ys
L_Halpha to L_acc relation of Rigliaco et al. 2012, then L_acc ∝ G M Mdot / R
assumptions: A_V ~0.4 mag for A; no extinction correction for B; A's R mag 11.0 from literature

recipe.goal: Tidal truncation constraint on GQ Lup B orbit
recipe.method: Eggleton/Pichardo truncation radius formula compared to 46.5 AU disk radius for orbit groups
assumptions: Secondary mass 25 MJup; disk radius 46.5 AU

evidence.quote: We measured a flux of $27.5\pm0.6$ mJy for this source.

answer_key.quantity: GQ Lup A dust mass (Model A)
Surface density index gamma (Model A / B)
GQ Lup B disk dust mass upper limit

evidence.quote: our data put a upper limit on the disk mass for GQ Lup B at $<$0.25–1 $M_\ensuremath{\oplus}$ from a point source to 1/3 of the Hill radius
GQ Lup B was detected in H$\alpha$ at S/N $\sim$ 6.3 with a contrast of 8.60 $\pm$ 0.16 mag.

evidence.loc: MagAO Astrometry of GQ Lup B
evidence.quote: GQ Lup B is 0.721$''$ $\pm$ 0.003$''$ from its host star, with a position angle of 277.6$^\circ$ $\pm$ 0.4$^\circ$

evidence.loc: Derivation of Accretion Rates from H$\alpha$ Fluxes
evidence.quote: The resulting accretion rates for GQ Lup A and B are $\dot{M}\sim10^{-8}$ to $10^{-7}~M_\ensuremath{\odot}~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$

not_stated_but_needed: Channel-selection and mask details for CLEAN and self-calibration solution intervals
Priors, parameter ranges, number of steps and burn-in for emcee fits
Fixed parameters in RADMC-3D (photon counts, grid, distance, stellar mass)
Source-finding routine details for the fake-source injection
missing_for_reproduction: emcee priors, bounds and chain lengths
score_reason: ALMA data identified and imaging described, but key fitting and CASA parameters are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data, an explicit recipe for imaging and disk fitting, and numeric results in Table 2.
